_comment: Site survey test vectors, checked by both implementations: web/js/survey.js (tests/web/unit/survey.test.js) and tools/gatelink_client/survey.py (tests/tools/test_survey.py). Numbers compare to 1e-9; texts exactly. Regenerate the expected values only after checking a change by hand: they are the specification.

cases.name: good: strong link, the SNR saturated, room capped by the tx_power minimum
cases.headline: Good: the weaker direction (at the house) keeps 67.5 dB above the SF9 limit in 90 % of pings (good from 15 dB, fair from 10 dB).
advice: Plenty of margin. If you like, tx_power (17 dBm on this board) could be lowered by up to 15 dB on both boards and still keep 15 dB.

cases.name: good: on the gate, the peer judged by SNR alone, room limited by the margin
cases.headline: Good: the weaker direction (at the house) keeps 17.4 dB above the SF9 limit in 90 % of pings (good from 15 dB, fair from 10 dB).
advice: Plenty of margin. If you like, tx_power (17 dBm on this board) could be lowered by up to 2 dB on both boards and still keep 15 dB.

cases.name: fair: the weaker direction's 10th percentile exactly 10 dB
cases.headline: Fair: the weaker direction (at the gate) keeps 10.0 dB above the SF10 limit in 90 % of pings (good from 15 dB, fair from 10 dB).
advice: Usable, with less than 15 dB in hand for rain, foliage and interference. If it is easy, mount the antennas higher with a clearer line of sight between the boards, and survey again.

cases.name: marginal: tx_power and sf at their limits
cases.headline: Marginal: the weaker direction (at the gate) keeps 7.0 dB above the SF12 limit in 90 % of pings (good from 15 dB, fair from 10 dB).
advice: Mount the antennas higher, clear of metal, walls and the relay shield, with as clear a line of sight between the boards as you can get: that gains more than any setting.
tx_power and sf are at their limits: only antenna placement, or a higher-gain antenna, can help.
Then run the survey again.

cases.name: good: 4 % lost (2 of 50) is chance, under the 5 % limit; the loss note shows
cases.headline: Good: the weaker direction (at the gate) keeps 31.5 dB above the SF9 limit in 90 % of pings (good from 15 dB, fair from 10 dB).
advice: Frames are being lost: check the antennas and their cables, and both boards' noise floor for interference.
Plenty of margin. If you like, tx_power (10 dBm on this board) could be lowered by up to 8 dB on both boards and still keep 15 dB.

cases.name: poor: 6 % unanswered (3 of 50), though the margin is good
cases.headline: Poor: 6.0 % of pings went unanswered (more than 5.0 %), though the weaker direction (at the gate) keeps 31.5 dB above the SF9 limit in 90 % of pings.
advice: Frames are being lost: check the antennas and their cables, and both boards' noise floor for interference.
Mount the antennas higher, clear of metal, walls and the relay shield, with as clear a line of sight between the boards as you can get: that gains more than any setting.
Raise tx_power (10 dBm on this board, at most 20) on both boards, each on a solid supply: a weak one can reset the board at full power.
Or raise sf (now 9) on BOTH boards, as radio settings must match or the link stops: each step adds about 2.5 dB of margin and roughly doubles the airtime.
Then run the survey again.

cases.name: good: one ping lost of 20 (5 %) is chance; few answers and the loss note show
cases.headline: Good: the weaker direction (at the gate) keeps 31.5 dB above the SF9 limit in 90 % of pings (good from 15 dB, fair from 10 dB).
advice: Only 19 pings were answered: run the survey longer for a firmer result.
Frames are being lost: check the antennas and their cables, and both boards' noise floor for interference.
Plenty of margin. If you like, tx_power (10 dBm on this board) could be lowered by up to 8 dB on both boards and still keep 15 dB.

cases.name: good: exactly 2 % lost and exactly 15 dB, tx_power at its minimum
cases.headline: Good: the weaker direction (at the gate) keeps 15.0 dB above the SF9 limit in 90 % of pings (good from 15 dB, fair from 10 dB).
advice: Plenty of margin: nothing to change.

cases.name: fair: only five pings answered
cases.headline: Fair: the weaker direction (at the house) keeps 10.0 dB above the SF8 limit in 90 % of pings (good from 15 dB, fair from 10 dB).
advice: Only 5 pings were answered: run the survey longer for a firmer result.
Usable, with less than 15 dB in hand for rain, foliage and interference. If it is easy, mount the antennas higher with a clearer line of sight between the boards, and survey again.

cases.name: poor: nothing answered
cases.headline: Poor: 100.0 % of pings went unanswered (more than 5.0 %).
advice: Frames are being lost: check the antennas and their cables, and both boards' noise floor for interference.
Mount the antennas higher, clear of metal, walls and the relay shield, with as clear a line of sight between the boards as you can get: that gains more than any setting.
Raise tx_power (17 dBm on this board, at most 20) on both boards, each on a solid supply: a weak one can reset the board at full power.
Or raise sf (now 9) on BOTH boards, as radio settings must match or the link stops: each step adds about 2.5 dB of margin and roughly doubles the airtime.
Then run the survey again.

cases.name: no result: no pings sent
cases.headline: No result: no pings were sent.
advice: Run the survey with the link up.

cases.name: good: no peer levels in the pongs
cases.headline: Good: the weaker direction (at the house) keeps 21.5 dB above the SF9 limit in 90 % of pings (good from 15 dB, fair from 10 dB).
advice: Plenty of margin. If you like, tx_power (17 dBm on this board) could be lowered by up to 6 dB on both boards and still keep 15 dB.
